root_cause: Recent provider history showed few schedule-triggered executions of the one Recovery Supervisor compared with its existing five-minute cron. GitHub docs say scheduled Actions can be delayed/dropped under high load, especially at top of hour. Provider-side actor/dispatch availability and causal mechanism remain unconfirmed.

evidence.baseline_manual_or_dispatch_not_schedule: workflow_dispatch run 39960974891 on merged CAS main is not independent cron liveness proof

fix: Retain exactly one existing Recovery Supervisor and five-minute interval; move native schedule from minute 0,5,...,55 to minute 2,7,...,57. Commit cron configuration to main via strict PR controls and avoid top-of-hour load while retaining native expected-head CAS, one writer, bounded retries, CI and release checks.
prevention_rule: A schedule declaration and manual workflow_dispatch do not prove actual scheduler liveness. Measure real GitHub event=schedule starts and successful completions across representative time windows; do not claim 100% scheduling or auto-recovery without observed provider evidence.

invariants: no added schedule or push fanout
